hypothesis: If the paired horns of hollow-horned ruminants are mirror-image conjugate spirals, then after reflecting one side's horn landmarks across the skull midsagittal plane and Procrustes-superimposing, the left and right horn shapes of the same individual differ by no more than the digitizing error.
pass_criterion: Using only bovid (hollow-horned) specimens that have homologous horn-core landmarks on both sides, the median Procrustes distance between each reflected left horn configuration and its right counterpart is at most 2% of centroid size. Fewer than 10% of specimens have an individual asymmetry above 5% of centroid size. In a Procrustes ANOVA (side x individual), directional asymmetry explains less than 5% of the shape variance.
fail_criterion: The median reflected-left versus right Procrustes distance exceeds 5% of centroid size, or more than 25% of bovid specimens exceed 5% asymmetry. Alternatively, the directional-asymmetry term in the Procrustes ANOVA is significant (p<0.01) and explains at least 10% of the shape variance, so the horns are not mirror images. If the dataset contains no bilateral horn-core landmarks, the test is undecidable and is reported as such, not as a pass.
interpretation: Thompson's 'conjugate spirals' and 'mirror-image' are read as: the left horn's 3D shape equals the right horn's shape after reflection across the midsagittal plane. His 'hollow-horned ruminants' are Bovidae, so Cervidae antlers in the dataset are excluded. Modern reinterpretation: horn spirality is measured through bilateral landmarks on horn cores, not fitted logarithmic spirals. This tests mirror symmetry of landmark shape, which is necessary but not sufficient for exact spiral conjugacy. The landmark data derive from Haber (2016), cited by the Dryad record. The landing page does not say which landmarks are horn landmarks, so the README and data.zip must be inspected before analysis.

dataset.name: Data: Diversification of the ruminant skull along an evolutionary line of least resistance
dataset.publisher: Dryad (data author Daniel Rhoda, University of Chicago)
dataset.why_it_fits: It holds raw landmark coordinates (data.zip, 74.9 MB) for 2,859 ruminant skulls, with R scripts and a README. Bovid specimens carrying bilateral horn-core landmarks would let me reflect one side and compare it with the other. The landing page does not confirm that horn landmarks exist or that they are bilateral. This must be checked in the README and data.zip, and if absent the test is undecidable.
